## Goal

Determine how often the llama-proxy flips between **fast** and **cheap** modes,
what triggers each flip (in particular the ContextHub/herdr code that initiates
the switch to fast), whether the flip rate is problematic, and what (if
anything) should change to reduce it.

## Context / findings so far

Investigation of the 24h window 2026-10-14 14:02 → 2026-10-15 14:02 UTC found
**30 proxy restarts**, of which **15 were "Mode-switch restart spawned"**
(one restart per real mode transition).

Trigger sources identified:

- **ContextHub / herdr** — `../ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`:
  - *Fast on command*: records operator activity and fire-and-forget
    `POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}`.
  - *Cheap on idle*: leader-only, when idle ≥
    `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (900_000 ms = 15 min) **and** the
    proxy reports idle, gated by the model-cooldown signal.
  - Shared activity broadcast via `mode-activity.json`; leader elected via the
    downtime worker; fail-closed everywhere.
- **Proxy's built-in time schedule** — `proxy/mode_schedule.yaml`
  (cheap 01:00, fast 10:00) = 2/day.
- **Manual** `POST /admin/set-mode` (operators/agents).

Each real transition persists the mode and spawns
`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart` (`proxy/proxy/mode.py` `set_mode()` →
`_spawn_restart()`), because fast/cheap are separate config profiles
(`config-fast.yaml` vs `config-cheap.yaml`) with different slot-pool sizes
(fast: base `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; cheap: 3). The restart re-inits
llama-server and typically yields a ~60s local-qwen3 cooldown on a cold-start
503. Redundant switches are skipped (mode already matches), so transition count
== restart-contribution count.

**Is this period unusual?** Historical per-calendar-day mode-switch counts from
the rotated logs: 10-08=28, 10-09=22, 10-10=16, 10-11=10, 10-12=32, 10-13=24,
10-14=31, 10-15=19 (partial, ~14h). So flipping is **endemic (~10–34/day)** —
to be confirmed and extended in this investigation.

## Questions to answer

1. How many flips/day, split by trigger source (ContextHub fast-on-command,
   ContextHub idle-cheap, proxy schedule, manual)?
2. Is the fast-on-command path firing repeatedly during active periods
   (flip-flop)? Quantify fast→cheap→fast pairs within short windows.
3. What is the cost per flip (restart duration, local cooldown, dropped or
   retried in-flight work, cold-prefill thunder)?
4. What else (besides mode) causes the proxy to restart, and how much of the
   flip rate is attributable to each?
5. What options exist to reduce flipping (e.g. minimum-dwell/hysteresis, keep
   fast during working hours rather than idle-cheap, only switch when the
   benefit is real, coalesce/defer switches, non-destructive switch), with
   trade-offs?
6. Recommendation: act or not, and if so, what and with what measurable target?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Flip frequency over ≥7 days of logs is documented (per-day counts +
      intra-day distribution), separated by trigger source.
- [ ] The ContextHub `mode-switch-worker.ts` switching logic is documented
      (triggers, gates, thresholds, leader election, cooldown gate, fail-closed
      behaviour).
- [ ] A quantified answer to "was the studied 24h period unusual?" against the
      ≥7-day baseline.
- [ ] A cost-per-flip estimate (restart duration, local cooldown, in-flight
      impact, cold-prefill effect).
- [ ] A prioritised list of reduction options with expected effect and
      trade-offs, and at least one recommended option with a measurable target.
- [ ] Follow-up implementation work items are created for the recommended
      option(s), or a decision not to act is recorded.
- [ ] Evidence is command/log based and reproducible (exact greps/scripts
      recorded in this item).

## References

- Related items: LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX (time-based schedule),
  LP-0MSMF5LXO006YDNM (in-flight sessions across mode switches),
  LP-0MSMFQ3DL006EY2H (grandfathered routing tests).
- Code: `proxy/proxy/mode.py`, `proxy/mode_schedule.yaml`,
  `../ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`.
- Logs: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`.
data.title: Investigate fast<->cheap proxy mode-flip frequency and how to reduce it (ContextHub trigger focus)

# Intake brief: Equalise fast/cheap slot counts (3/2/1) or keep the drain

Work item: LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5 — Priority: medium — Type: task

## Problem statement

Switching between **fast** and **cheap** modes currently restarts the whole
proxy **and** llama-server, because the two profiles differ in
`session_slot_pool_size` (fast/base = 1, cheap = 3). The restart discards the
warm KV cache and kills in-flight local streams. We need to know whether a
single slot count is viable for both modes — which would let a switch keep the
running llama-server (via the existing adopt/reuse path) — or whether the
per-mode slot count must stay and the already-implemented drain remains the
mitigation.

## Users

- **Agent operators / users** — long-running Pi sessions through the proxy; a
  mode switch today interrupts work and loses the warm cache, degrading the
  next requests' TTFT.
- **Proxy operators** — switch modes manually (UI/API) or on schedule
  (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00) and want the switch to be cheap and
  non-disruptive.
- **Benchmark / maintainer** — needs reproducible numbers to justify (or
  reject) a config change.

User stories:

- As an agent operator, I want a mode switch to preserve the warm local KV
  cache so my next request is not slowed by a cold restart.
- As a proxy operator, I want an evidence-based decision on whether fast and
  cheap can share one slot count, so the restart-on-switch can be removed (or
  knowingly retained).
- As a maintainer, I want the 1/2/3-slot trade-off quantified (per-slot
  context, memory, decode speed, contention) for the small-request workload the
  local slot actually serves.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Benchmark results for 1, 2 and 3 slots are recorded with reproducible
   commands, configs and raw numbers, covering throughput, latency/TTFT,
   queue-timeout / `fallback_after_queue` rate, local stream share, and local
   quarantine episodes, at ≥ the observed concurrency (2–3 concurrent sessions
   plus queue depth).
2. A recommendation states whether a single slot count is viable for both
   modes, the chosen N, and the measured trade-offs (per-slot context, memory,
   decode speed, contention including queue-timeout rate).
3. The evaluation explicitly accounts for large-context bypass traffic
   (400–750/day, `large_context_bypass` / `context_too_large`) when interpreting
   the per-slot context trade-off — i.e. how much of the local-eligible traffic
   is small, and what per-slot context can be given up at higher N.
4. If a single slot count is viable: a follow-up work item is created to
   converge `session_slot_pool_size` across
   `config.yaml` / `config-fast.yaml` / `config-cheap.yaml` and make the switch
   non-destructive by reusing the running llama-server (existing adopt path,
   LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN) rather than restarting it.
5. If not viable: the recommendation documents why, confirms the
   already-implemented bounded drain (`server.mode_switch_drain`,
   LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE) remains the mitigation, and files any gaps found as
   follow-up items (`discovered-from:LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5`).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- The proxy serves concurrent production consumers; the benchmark must not
  permanently destabilise the running config. Any config edit during
  benchmarking must be reverted/restored, and the proxy left in the correct
  scheduled mode.
- Slot count must match llama-server `--parallel`; changing it requires a
  llama-server restart (the very cost under evaluation).
- fast = 1 slot × 262144 ctx; cheap = 3 slots × 262144 ctx. Per-slot context at
  N slots is roughly `ctx_size // N` minus output headroom (routing thresholds
  are auto-derived; see config comments).
- Benchmark scripts/artifacts live under `proxy/benchmarks/`; transient outputs
  must not leave tracked paths permanently dirty.

## Existing state

- `proxy/config.yaml` (base profile) `session_slot_pool_size: 1`;
  `proxy/config-fast.yaml` overrides other values but inherits 1;
  `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` sets `session_slot_pool_size: 3`.
- A mode switch is a full restart (`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart`)
  driven by `proxy/proxy/mode.py`; it also restarts llama-server, so the warm
  KV cache is lost.
- A **bounded drain already exists** (`mode.py`: `_begin_drain`, `draining()`,
  `drain_retry_after()`, `_count_in_flight_local_streams()`,
  `_wait_for_in_flight_local_streams()`, `_spawn_restart`), implemented under
  LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE (completed) and covered by
  `proxy/tests/test_mode_switch_drain.py`. It defers new chat requests
  (503 + Retry-After) and waits up to `mode_switch_drain.max_seconds`
  (fast 30s, cheap/base 90s). ⇒ the item's conditional "implement a drain"
  branch is already satisfied.
- llama-server reuse/adopt across a proxy-only restart exists in
  `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` (LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN), with
  `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` `merged_config_sha256` guarding against
  adopting a stale config.
- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` (LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD) varies
  1/2/4/6/8/12 slots and measures throughput/latency/TTFT/GPU memory. It does
  **not** currently report queue-timeout rate, local stream share, or
  quarantine episodes, and uses 6 concurrent requests — it may need extension
  for the concurrency/metrics this item requires.
- Contention evidence carried in the item: fast 1-slot 10:00–14:02 window →
  173 `fallback_after_queue`; cheap 3-slot 01:00–10:00 → 207 over a longer
  window; 39 `empty_response` cooldowns cluster under 1-slot contention.

## Desired change

Produce an evidence-backed verdict on a single slot count for both modes and
act on it:

- **Viable** → create a follow-up item to converge the configs and keep
  llama-server warm across the switch (adopt path); the mode switch becomes a
  proxy-only restart.
- **Not viable** → document why and keep the existing bounded drain; file any
  gaps as `discovered-from` follow-ups.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — base profile; `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; routing and
  context thresholds.
- `proxy/config-fast.yaml` — fast overlay; inherits slot count, sets
  `mode_switch_drain.max_seconds: 30`.
- `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — cheap overlay; `session_slot_pool_size: 3`.
- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — existing slot sweep; candidate to
  extend with queue-timeout / local-share / quarantine metrics.
- `proxy/proxy/mode.py` — mode switch, bounded drain, `_spawn_restart`.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — llama-server reuse/adopt across proxy restart
  (LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN).
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — `deep_merge` + `merged_config_sha256`
  stale-adopt guard.
- `proxy/tests/test_mode_switch_drain.py` — existing drain test coverage.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` — existing benchmark unit tests.

## Related work

- LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD — Slot-count benchmark: optimal `session_slot_pool_size`
  (completed; script reusable).
- LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE — Drain or re-route in-flight local streams at
  mode-switch restart (completed; drain implemented).
- LP-0MT60S55M000TK1H — Stream finish errors: recover-first reroute (completed;
  classified 4 restart-kill events).
- LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN — llama-server reuse across proxy-only restarts (adopt).
- LP-0MRW0WTOO002GG8I — pool 2 → 6 (completed).
- LP-0MQMH0WHY005UPFA — align pool with llama-server `--parallel`.
- LP-0MRDE669Y003V1SO — cache-cold after restart.
- LP-0MSM3TGO3007QN9M — mode control UI.
- LP-0MSMF5LXO006YDNM — in-flight sessions keep their models across mode
  switches (completed).
- LP-0MU5BOK3P0090O0V — mode flapping / switch restarts (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the benchmark can be run without permanently disrupting
  production; the config is restored and the proxy left in the correct
  scheduled mode afterwards.
- **Assumption:** the already-implemented bounded drain satisfies the item's
  conditional "if not viable: implement a drain" branch (see Existing state),
  so the remaining scope is evaluation → recommendation → follow-up items.
- **Risk:** benchmarking 3 × 262144 ctx may OOM or force a lower per-slot
  context, biasing results. Record memory and per-slot context, and treat
  OOM / severely reduced per-slot context as a viability failure.
- **Risk:** the benchmark workload may not match real traffic — large-context
  bypass dominates request counts but never touches the local slot. Characterise
  the local-eligible request mix explicitly.
- **Risk (scope creep):** tuning the drain, changing remote fallback policy, or
  UI changes are **out of scope** here — record as linked follow-up items
  rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (prior mode-flip
investigation) plus repository inspection (`mode.py`, `lifecycle.py`,
`config*.yaml`, `proxy/benchmarks/`, `proxy/tests/`) sufficed to draft the
brief. One interpretation was recorded as a documented assumption (see Risks &
assumptions): the already-implemented bounded drain satisfies the item's
conditional "implement a drain" branch, so the remaining work is evaluation →
recommendation → follow-up items.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MU6MQIPP0058198** – Add fast→cheap mode-switch cooldown to stop flip-flopping (completed)
- **LP-0MT1EE315007AKXG** – proxy-usage-analysis: recognize manual mode switches in mode timeline (completed)
- **LP-0MU5BOK3P0090O0V** – Proxy mode flapping: four mode-switch restarts in 5 minutes at the 10:00 schedule boundary (herdr set-mode suspected) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, accounts, active, align, already (+143 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: acceptance, accounts, active, align, already (+143 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: acceptance, accounts, active, align, already (+143 more)
data.title: Evaluate performance impact of equalising fast/cheap slot counts (3/2/1); if not viable implement a drain

data.description:
# Implement grace-period immunity: local cold-start 503s must not trigger a 60s local cooldown

## Problem statement

After a proxy restart, local (Qwen3) requests that race llama-server warm-up receive HTTP 503 and are treated identically to genuine failures — applying the standard `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60` quarantine and feeding the failure counter. This causes the dominant source of ~60s local quarantines (~12 of 45 episodes in one 24h window), even though the 503 reflects "not ready yet" rather than a provider fault.

## Users

- **Local-proxy operator:** wants the proxy to recover immediately after a restart without wasting up to 60s of requests per restart.
- **Pi-extension / end-user:** experiences dropped requests or latency spikes during restarts.

## User stories

- As a proxy operator, when llama-server is cold after a restart, a local request that receives HTTP 503 should defer (Retry-After) without quarantining the provider.
- As a proxy operator, when local continues to return HTTP 503 **after** the warm-up window, the standard cooldown should still apply (genuine faults not masked).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A deterministic unit test reproduces the current cold-start 503 → 60s cooldown, then verifies it no longer occurs after the change.
2. Tests cover:
   - (a) Cold-start 503 within the `is_cold()` warm-up window → defer via Retry-After, no cooldown, no failure-counter bump.
   - (b) Sustained HTTP 503 **after** the warm-up window ends → normal cooldown applies.
   - (c) Connection error during warm-up → defer, no cooldown.
   - (d) Concurrent cold-start dispatch gating (`local_cold_start_max_concurrent`) still respected.
   - (e) A fresh warm-up window begins after each restart (new `note_model_loaded()` arms it).
3. The exponential-backoff failure counter is not polluted during the warm-up window.
4. No regression in routing/fallback tests; full suite passes via `/skill:test` before commit.
5. Follows the implement workflow (worktree, build → test → commit).
6. Logs/metrics evidence pre/post: local cooldown episodes in the hour after a restart drop to ~0.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments in `cold_start.py`/`provider.py`, `proxy/config.yaml` knobs, and any relevant docs entries (e.g. `proxy/docs/`).

## Constraints

- **Reuse `cold_start.is_cold()` as the single immunity-boundary signal.** No new window plumbing. The existing grace window already bounds the immunity period and is self-expiring.
- **Only HTTP 503 + connection errors defer during the window.** All other 5xx during warm-up still quarantine — a genuine sustained non-503 fault is still quarantined.
- **Behaviour applies per restart event.** A new `note_model_loaded()` call arms a fresh warm-up window.
- **Must interact correctly with existing concurrent cold-start dispatch gating** (`local_cold_start_max_concurrent`).
- **No magic sleeps.** The readiness/warm-up signal is explicit and bounded.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: masking genuine local faults.** Mitigated by deferring only HTTP 503 + connection errors, and only while `is_cold()` is True — any other 5xx or post-window 503 still quarantines.
- **Risk: window not armed when 503s arrive.** If some warm-up 503s occur before `note_model_loaded()` arms the window, immunity will not cover them; verifiable in tests/logs, and if a gap exists it becomes a follow-up (not in scope here).
- **Risk: deferral storm.** Deferring during cold-start must respect the existing `local_cold_start_max_concurrent` gating so a burst of deferred requests does not accumulate unboundedly.
- **Assumption:** `is_cold()` semantics (armed at model load, self-expiring grace window) are the correct boundary; per Q1 this was confirmed by the operator.
- **Scope creep guard:** extending immunity to other status codes, other providers, or re-architecting the cold-start state machine is **out of scope** — record as separate work items if discovered.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` — manages a bounded cold-start grace window: `note_model_loaded()`, `mark_warm()`, `is_cold()`, `note_backend_down()`. Config: `local_cold_start_grace_seconds` (default 120), `local_cold_start_max_concurrent` (default 1), `local_cold_start_retry_after_seconds` (default 15).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown()` (line ~4871) calls `mark_provider_unavailable()` for all HTTP errors including 503; `_handle_connection_error_in_fallback()` (line ~4832) does the same for connection errors. Exponential backoff only applies to remote providers.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — denies concurrent local dispatches during cold (`is_cold()` check), logs `local_dispatch_denied ... cold_start=True`.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60` (line 581).

## Desired change

- In `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown()` and `_handle_connection_error_in_fallback()`, check `cold_start.is_cold(config)`. If cold and the error is HTTP 503 or a connection error, **do not** call `mark_provider_unavailable()` or bump the failure counter. Instead, defer the request (return Retry-After using `cold_start.retry_after_seconds(config)`), and set an appropriate fallback reason.
- The deferred request should behave like a `Retry-After` signal to the caller (existing mechanism already supports this).
- A non-503 HTTP error (e.g., 500, 502) during the window should still call `mark_provider_unavailable()` to avoid masking genuine faults.
- A non-connection error during the window still quarantines normally.

## Key files

- `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` — read `is_cold()`, `retry_after_seconds()` for immunity decision.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown()` (~4871), `_handle_connection_error_in_fallback()` (~4832), `mark_provider_unavailable()` (~2141).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — cold-start dispatch gating (line ~1086) — verify no interaction conflicts.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `note_model_loaded()` call sites (~230, ~2007, ~2042, ~2222) — confirm window is armed before first 503s.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — cold-start config knobs.
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_admission.py` — existing cold-start admission test suite; add the grace-period immunity cases here (or a sibling test module).
- `proxy/README.md` — update cooldown/cold-start documentation.

## Related work

### Related work items
- **LP-0MR01SJBP005I0OR** — "Fallback not recovering after model-loading 503; returns all providers exhausted" (completed). Sibling investigation.
- **LP-0MUCEEZ6B003NZH5** — "Restart-resilient local dispatch: prevent post-restart pool wedge from no-progress prefills" (completed). Parent epic / adjacent.
- **LP-0MPY3DGGF0042178** — "proxyctl: restart command" (completed). Restart tooling context.
- **LP-0MRE4NBQ5009V5BX** — "Add dual-threshold large-context routing bypass (cold-cache + warm-cache)" (completed). Cold/warm routing interaction.
- **LP-0MUYN2RD800889S2** — "[test-failure] tests/test_cold_start_admission.py::test_proxy_to_local_warm_bypasses_cold_cap — failing test" (completed). Existing cold-start admission test suite.

### Investigation context
- **LP-0MV9UNE75004903J** — mode-flip frequency investigation (restart-frequency context).
- **LP-0MV9UNKVK007TN7E** — proxy restart frequency examination (restart causes).

### Repository references
- `proxy/README.md` — cold-start / cooldown documentation surface.
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_admission.py` — existing cold-start admission tests (extend for immunity cases).

## Appendix

- Q: Where should the immunity window anchor? — Answer (Map): Reuse `cold_start.is_cold()` as the single immunity-boundary signal (recommended option a).
- Q: Scope of deferred failures during the window? — Answer (Map): Strictly HTTP 503 + connection errors; all other 5xx still quarantine (recommended option a).
